This relatively protracted incubation, compared to open-cup nesting congeners, likely reflects the thermal constraints of the species' high-elevation Andean cloud forest habitat, where ambient temperatures can fluctuate dramatically. This annual reproductive output is notably conservative for a warbler, reflecting the energetic constraints of a montane lifestyle where the breeding season is sharply curtailed by the availability of insect prey. The combination of clutch size and clutch frequency yields a modest overall fecundity that is balanced against high adult survival.

Under standard laboratory conditions maintained at 41.6 °C [T = 41.6 °C], the time since birth at fledging for Citrine warbler nestlings is 13.5 days [tx = 13.5 days], marking the point at which flight feather maturation enables the fledgling to achieve its first flight and leave the nest.
